description: This donut chart, functioning as a pie chart with a hollow center, illustrates the distribution of a category identified by the bolded central text "Task Type." The chart displays a total of two slices. The significantly larger slice, colored light red, is labeled "Article generation" and accounts for 83.2% of the total. The smaller slice, colored yellow, is labeled "Headline generation" and represents the remaining 16.8%. The chart does not include a separate legend; rather, the category names and their exact percentages are presented as text labels positioned directly outside their corresponding segments. Neither of the slices is visually emphasized through exploding or offsetting. Visually, the segments are arranged such that the larger light red slice spans the majority of the ring from the top right around to the bottom, while the smaller yellow slice occupies the lower right section.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of task types across turns from verified Wildchat journalist-LLM conversations. The chart is divided into two categories: 'Article generation' and 'Headline generation.' Article generation accounts for approximately 73.2% of the total tasks, while headline generation constitutes 26.8%. The chart highlights a significant decline in headline generation tasks compared to article generation, suggesting a shift in focus toward more comprehensive content creation. The slices are arranged in descending order by size, with the title 'Task Type' displayed centrally within the chart.
